the TP53 mutation prevalence among early-onset breast cancers in a large cohort of young breast cancer patients was low (2.2%), and the majority of these patients did not have additional features suggestive of LFS.

2.2% of young breast cancer patients carry a (likely pathogenic) TP53 germlin mutation, that 2.0% of women with early-onset breast and no family history suggestive of Li-Fraumeni syndrome carry a (likely patogenic) TP53 mutation, and that the prevalence of TP53 mutations in early onset breast cancer is comparable or even higher to the prevalence of TP543 mutations in older breast cancer patients.

a very low TP53 mutation prevalence among BRCA1/2 mutation negative young patients without a suggestive family history or personal history of multiple cancers.
the fact that the prevalence of germline TP53 mutations in women diagnosed with breast cancers at very young ages is low, and the clinical value of genetic testing in this setting is limited.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TP53 genetic counselling and testing in early-onest breast cancer patients should be considered on a case-by-case basis.
TP53 germlin testing is not indicated in women younger than 30 years with a BRCA1/2 negative breast cancer, without a suggestive family history and without additional tumour types.

TP53 mutation testing should be considered in young women (younger than 30 year old) with breast cancer and a strong family history suggestive for LFS, and in young breast cancer patients with a personal history of LFS-related tumour(s).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TP53 germlline mutation testing is indicated in women with early-onset breast cancers, especially when there is a personal or family history suggestive for LFS.
TP53 mutation testing should be considered in women with a personal or family history of LFS-related cancers, regardless of age.
a young age of breast cancer onset is a risk factor for a TP53 mutation and should be taken into account in the decision to perform TP53 genetic testing.
